entries.headline: Bastion Square Partners II raises $1.5 million in its TSX Venture debut
entries.dek: The Vancouver capital pool company sold 15 million shares at 10 cents each and will look for an acquisition target to complete its qualifying transaction.
entries.caption: Downtown Vancouver across False Creek.

sources.title: Bastion Square Partners II Inc. Closes Initial Public Offering and Lists on the TSX Venture Exchange as a Capital Pool Company
Bastion Square Partners II Inc. (BASQ.P) Raises $1.5 Million in IPO, Lists on TSX Venture Exchange as Capital Pool Company

brief: Bastion Square Partners II Inc., a Vancouver-based capital pool company, closed its initial public offering on November 3, 2026, raising $1.5 million in gross proceeds through the sale of 15,000,000 common shares at $0.10 each. The shares listed on the TSX Venture Exchange that day under a trading halt pending closing.

Trading in the shares, under the symbol BASQ.P, is set to resume November 9, 2026. The company now has 27,000,000 shares outstanding, of which 13,825,000 are held in escrow. Independent Trading Group (ITG), Inc. acted as agent, earning a $55,000 cash commission, a $10,000 corporate finance fee and 500,000 warrants exercisable at $0.10 until November 3, 2028.

Directors and officers were granted 2,700,000 incentive stock options at $0.10, exercisable for five years; directors also bought 1,825,000 of the offered shares themselves. The company has no business of its own: net proceeds will fund the search for an acquisition target to complete a qualifying transaction under TSX Venture Exchange rules.
body: Bastion Square Partners II Inc., a Vancouver-based capital pool company, closed its initial public offering on November 3, 2026, raising $1.5 million in gross proceeds through the sale of 15,000,000 common shares at $0.10 each. The TSX Venture Exchange approved the listing on November 2, and the shares began trading under a halt pending closing.

Trading in the shares, under the symbol BASQ.P, is scheduled to resume on November 9, 2026. Following the offering, the company has 27,000,000 common shares outstanding, of which 13,825,000 are held in escrow.

Independent Trading Group (ITG), Inc. acted as agent for the offering. It received a cash commission of $55,000, a corporate finance fee of $10,000, reimbursement of its legal fees and expenses, and 500,000 non-transferable warrants exercisable at $0.10 per share until November 3, 2028.

The company's directors and officers were granted 2,700,000 incentive stock options at an exercise price of $0.10, exercisable for five years. Directors also personally purchased 1,825,000 of the shares sold in the offering, a related-party transaction disclosed in the filing.

A capital pool company such as Bastion Square has no business or assets of its own beyond the cash raised at listing. Under TSX Venture Exchange rules, it must use the proceeds to identify and evaluate a business or asset to acquire, a process the exchange calls a qualifying transaction.

The release named Briony Bayer, the company's Chief Financial Officer and Corporate Secretary, as the contact for further information. It did not disclose any potential acquisition target or sector of interest.

entries.headline: Global Uranium raises its private placement minimum and adds a $1 million loan
entries.dek: The Calgary-based explorer increased the minimum subscription to $800,000 and secured a separate credit facility to fund its Saskatchewan and Wyoming uranium projects.
entries.caption: Eroded badlands in Wyoming.

sources.title: Global Uranium Announces Amended LIFE Offering and $1 Million Loan Facility
Global Uranium Corp (GURN) Revises LIFE Offering and Secures $1M Unsecured Loan Facility

brief: Global Uranium Corp. filed an amended offering document on November 3, 2026 for its non-brokered private placement under the listed issuer financing exemption, raising the minimum subscription to 3,636,364 units for gross proceeds of $800,000.08. The maximum remains 4,239,711 units for $932,736.42, both at $0.22 per unit, with closing expected on or about November 6, 2026.

Each unit comprises one common share and one warrant exercisable at $0.30, not available until 61 days after closing and expiring 24 months after closing. Separately, the company entered a committed, unsecured, non-revolving loan facility of up to $1,000,000 with an arm's-length lender, charging 12% simple annual interest, with no amount drawn as of the announcement.

Advances may be drawn until October 30, 2028 on five business days' notice, with each advance due 24 months later and all amounts owed by November 3, 2030. The company said proceeds from both will fund exploration and option payments on its Astro project in Saskatchewan and its Wyoming projects, plus working capital.
body: Global Uranium Corp. (CSE: GURN; OTCQB: GURFF) filed an amended and restated offering document on November 3, 2026 for its non-brokered private placement under the listed issuer financing exemption (LIFE). The minimum subscription was increased to 3,636,364 units for gross proceeds of $800,000.08; the maximum offering remains 4,239,711 units for $932,736.42, both at an unchanged price of $0.22 per unit.

Each unit comprises one common share and one warrant exercisable at $0.30 per share. The warrant does not become exercisable until 61 days after closing and expires 24 months after closing. Closing is expected on or about November 6, 2026, subject to regulatory approvals including those of the Canadian Securities Exchange.

The release said the securities are expected to be immediately freely tradable under applicable Canadian securities laws, subject to the restrictions that apply to control persons, and that the offering is available to purchasers in Canada other than Quebec and New Brunswick.

Separately, the Calgary-based uranium explorer entered a committed, unsecured, non-revolving loan facility of up to $1,000,000 with an arm's-length lender. Advances can be requested on five business days' notice until October 30, 2028, each carrying 12% simple annual interest and due for repayment 24 months after it is drawn, with all amounts owed no later than November 3, 2030. No funds had been drawn as of the announcement.

The facility carries no demand-repayment clause and allows prepayment without penalty, the company said. Proceeds from both the placement and the facility are earmarked for exploration expenditures and option payments on the company's Astro uranium project in Saskatchewan and its Wyoming projects in the Great Divide Basin, Gas Hills and Copper Mountain districts, as well as corporate liabilities, administration and working capital.
The release does not name the arm's-length lender, and does not name an agent for the private placement.

brief: Advanced Micro Devices recorded a $1.07 billion non-cash charge, or 66 cents a share, in the third quarter ended September 26, tied to warrants it issued to OpenAI and Meta Platforms as part of multibillion-dollar AI chip supply agreements.

body: Advanced Micro Devices recorded a $1.07 billion non-cash charge, equal to 66 cents a share, in the third quarter ended September 26. The charge relates to warrants the chipmaker has issued to OpenAI and Meta Platforms as part of multibillion-dollar agreements to supply them with AI chips.

Under a February agreement, AMD agreed to sell Meta up to $60 billion of AI chips over five years. Meta received warrants allowing it to buy as much as 10% of AMD if certain shipment milestones are met.

AMD shares rose 8% in extended trading after the results, and the company forecast 2027 growth faster than previously expected. Bob O'Donnell, chief analyst at TECHnalysis Research, said of the broader trend of chipmakers issuing customer warrants: "While I do believe incentives played a role in some of their sales, I believe the bigger issue is that there is pent-up demand for a serious alternative to Nvidia."

AMD is not alone in using warrants to secure large AI customers. Cerebras has granted OpenAI warrants against a $20 billion commitment, Marvell issued Google warrants for a potential $12.2 billion stake, and Qualcomm gave Amazon warrants as part of a $60 billion deal, according to the report.

On Canada's venture boards, the artificial intelligence and data-centre theme comprises 29 listed names; 16 traded today, 6 higher and 5 lower, for a median move of +0.00% against -0.77% for the S&P/TSX Venture Composite, a spread of 0.77 percentage points in the theme's favour.

Sparc AI Inc. (CSE: SPAI) rose 0.99% to CAD2.04, and is in the theme because its registered name contains "ai". Predictiv AI Inc. (CSE: PAI) was unchanged at CAD0.105, also because its registered name contains "ai", as was Yocale.ai Inc. (CSE: YAI), unchanged at CAD0.74.

Roughly $55,000 of Sparc AI shares changed hands on the day, versus about $29,000 for Predictiv AI and $54,000 for Yocale.ai. AMD's results and the moves in these three Canadian venture names fell on the same day; nothing in either the company's statement or the quotes connects them, and no causal link is drawn here.

brief: Saudi Arabian Oil Co. reported third-quarter net profit of $36.25 billion, up 34% from a year earlier, as revenue climbed to $140.5 billion from $111.6 billion. The company attributed the increase to higher prices for crude oil and refined chemical products, even as sales volumes fell.

body: Saudi Arabian Oil Co. reported third-quarter net profit of $36.25 billion, up 34% from a year earlier, as revenue climbed to $140.5 billion from $111.6 billion over the same period. The company attributed the increase to higher prices for crude oil and refined chemical products, even as sales volumes fell.

The results followed attacks on Aramco's operations: Houthi militants from Yemen launched missile and drone strikes targeting company facilities, including its Dhahran headquarters and refining operations in Jazan and Riyadh, while Iranian activity in the Strait of Hormuz disrupted shipping. Chief executive Amin Nasser said: "Geopolitical uncertainty and attacks on key energy facilities continued to amplify the global energy supply crisis in the third quarter of 2026."

Aramco's board authorized a base dividend of $21.9 billion for the third quarter, up 3.5% from a year earlier and payable in the fourth quarter of 2026. Capital expenditure for the quarter totaled $10.5 billion, down from $12.6 billion a year earlier, and the company said it is pursuing additional overseas storage capacity and alternative export routes to help maintain supply reliability amid the disruptions.

On Canada's venture boards, the oil, gas and power theme comprises 72 listed venture names; 34 traded today, 12 higher and 11 lower, for a median move of +0.00% against -0.77% for the S&P/TSX Venture Composite, a spread of 0.77 percentage points.

The largest mover was Stamper Oil And Gas Corp (TSXV: STMP), up 40.00% to CAD0.14, followed by Reconnaissance Energy Africa Lt (TSXV: RECO), up 4.00% to CAD0.52; both are in the theme because their sector label is "Oil & Gas E&P". Among the decliners, Coelacanth Energy Inc (TSXV: CEI) fell 2.90% to CAD0.67, Lotus Creek Exploration Inc (TSXV: LTC) fell 1.77% to CAD4.43, and Robinson Energy Limited (TSXV: ROB) fell 1.52% to CAD3.24, each for the same reason.

Aramco's results and the moves among these five Canadian oil and gas names fell on the same calendar day. Nothing in either the company's release or the venture names' trading establishes a connection between the two, and none is drawn here.
